title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2

claim_as_stated: The manuscript claims μ(π)=2: for every fixed ν>2, all sufficiently large integer denominators q and all integer p satisfy |π−p/q|≥q^(−ν). It also claims convergence of Flint–Hills and the stated generalized sine-denominator criterion. It does not claim a uniform positive c/q² bound.
proof_architecture: Center-independent successively separated weighted interpolation supplies a nonzero full-row minor at rational approximate-period centers.
Truncated logarithms preserve the local weighted filtration and make entries Gaussian rational. Column/row denominator clearing gives a lower bound.
Translate the SAME rows to exact logarithmic periods. Within each transverse group, repeated Taylor degrees annihilate coefficient determinants and force quadratic collision saving.

Every expansion term either has many small transverse indices and large collisions, or many large indices and high powers of approximation errors. Full-simplex counts and coordinated high-dimensional parameters make both beat arithmetic costs.
Fix ν, dimension, weights, denominators and centers before the final polynomial-degree limit. A separate spacing argument converts the irrationality bound into sine-series convergence.
